title: Arbitrary Variation of Collection Traversal Syntax
pattern: Using different syntax styles to traverse collections across similar tasks in the same codebase.
why_bad: It increases reading friction. The reader has to pause to analyze whether there is a subtle memory-safety or performance reason for the syntactic difference, only to find it was arbitrary.
detection: Flag varying traversal syntax (loops, iterators, manual index ranges) across non-performance-critical paths.
counterexample: Using specific, non-standard iteration patterns because of concrete performance constraints or lifetime borrows. Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Standardize all standard collection iterations on the idiomatic `for item in &items` loops.
source: *Clean Code* by Robert C. Martin (2008), p. 292.
